Content:
I’ve got six big Case Logic binders and around 35 spindles—all loaded with pirated music and movies from the Rapidshare/Megaupload era. We all knew the record companies had their hands in our pockets back then, so grabbing what we could felt like payback.

But looking back, it came at a cost. Music lost its weight—what used to be meaningful became disposable. Beloved audio brands got stripped down and sold off, now just pumping out the next Bluetooth version like it’s progress.

I still collect records, tapes, CDs—there’s something real in that. But the culture that made it special? Gone. Even Bose doesn’t make wired speakers anymore. Not that they were amazing, but still… says a lot.

Author: @izimsi
Content:
This video just made me remember how we used to to download stuff in 100MB parts, sometimes like 45 of them (so a whole DVD). 
The most popular ISP in Poland used a dynamic IP assignment so usually you would just need to reset the connection to get a new IP and download the next part (because the site had a limit for free users).
In the peak times of piracy you sometimes needed to reset it a few times, because everyone else was doing the same thing, so you could run into another IP that someone just used to download something from RS or Mega.
